title: MED12 is overexpressed in glioblastoma patients and serves as an oncogene by targeting the VDR/BCL6/p53 axis.
authors: Srivastava, Srishti; Makala, Hima; Sharma, Vikas; Suri, Vaishali; Sarkar, Chitra; Kulshreshtha, Ritu
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
one_liner_zh: 该文研究胶质母细胞瘤中MED12过表达通过VDR/BCL6/p53轴发挥致癌作用，虽涉及MED12与VDR蛋白的对接和共免疫沉淀，但核心是肿瘤生物学与信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制，方法上仅简单对接，缺乏AI或物理模拟深度。
abstract: Glioblastoma is the most life-threatening tumor of the central nervous system. Despite recent therapeutic advancements, maximum survival of glioblastoma patients remains dismal. The mediator complex is a set of proteins, essential for eukaryotic gene expression. Abnormal expression/mutations of specific mediator genes have been associated with progression of various cancers, however, its role and status in glioblastoma remains largely unknown. Our work shows overexpression of a subunit of kinase assembly of mediator complex, MED12, in various glioblastoma patient cohorts including Indian glioblastoma patients and cell lines. Functional characterization of MED12 using both overexpression and knockdown approach revealed that it promotes glioblastoma cell proliferation, migration and inhibits apoptosis. Transcriptome analysis post MED12 knockdown revealed Vitamin D receptor (VDR) pathway to be one of the key pathways affected by MED12 in glioblastoma. We studied direct interaction of MED12 with VDR protein using docking studies and co-immunoprecipitation assay. We identify BCL6, a secondary regulator of VDR signaling, to be directly regulated by MED12 through a combination of chromatin immunoprecipitation, qRT-PCR and western analyses. We further show that MED12 brings about the inhibition of p53 levels and apoptosis partly through induction of BCL6 in glioblastoma. Overall, this stands as the first report of MED12 over-expression and involvement in glioblastoma pathogenesis and identifies MED12 as an important mediator of VDR signaling and an attractive molecule for development of new therapeutic interventions.
abstract_zh: 胶质母细胞瘤是中枢神经系统中最具生命威胁性的肿瘤。尽管近年来治疗有所进展，胶质母细胞瘤患者的最大生存期仍然不容乐观。中介体复合物是一组对真核基因表达至关重要的蛋白质。特定中介体基因的异常表达或突变与多种癌症的进展相关，然而其在胶质母细胞瘤中的作用和状态仍 largely 未知。我们的工作显示，中介体复合物激酶组装亚基 MED12 在多个胶质母细胞瘤患者队列中过表达，包括印度胶质母细胞瘤患者和细胞系。通过过表达和敲低方法对 MED12 进行功能表征，揭示其促进胶质母细胞瘤细胞增殖、迁移并抑制凋亡。MED12 敲低后的转录组分析显示，维生素D受体 (VDR) 通路是胶质母细胞瘤中受 MED12 影响的关键通路之一。我们通过对接研究和免疫共沉淀实验研究了 MED12 与 VDR 蛋白的直接相互作用。我们通过染色质免疫沉淀、qRT-PCR 和 Western 分析相结合，确定 VDR 信号传导的次级调节因子 BCL6 受 MED12 直接调控。我们进一步表明，MED12 部分通过诱导胶质母细胞瘤中的 BCL6 来抑制 p53 水平和凋亡。总体而言，这是关于 MED12 过表达及其参与胶质母细胞瘤发病机制的首份报告，并将 MED12 确定为 VDR 信号传导的重要中介体，以及开发新治疗干预措施的有吸引力的靶点。
